perItemFindings.one_line: Delivered tier incremental < floor field; directed reroute: Extend the frontier theorem from the homogeneous, engineered two-ellipsoid menu to arbitrary block-specific spectral triples and any finite number of classes, proving an exact polynomial-size LP reduction and an attaining independent-sign product law. review.verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=incremental below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The exact headline result is confined to two specially constructed homogeneous ellipsoids whose risks reduce, by design, to minimizing two affine functions over a three-point frequency simplex. The piecewise frontier and optimizer separation are therefore routine finite-dimensional consequences of standard maximin scalarization rather than a broadly usable robust-design theorem. The higher-rank result only enumerates the finite support in a standard exponential-column SDP, defines its relaxation gap as the difference of two computed optima, and adds a standard convex-support reduction; it supplies neither a new characterization nor a tractable algorithm. The Ryan–Esserman–Li separation is criterion-level algebra on the same constructed menu and does not establish a substantive limitation of that published design framework. The TL;DR and project justification accurately disclose these limitations, but the delivered content remains a routine special case rather than a field-level contribution.

DIRECTED IMPROVEMENT (re-derive the SAME object implementing this, do not reproduce the prior note): Extend the frontier theorem from the homogeneous, engineered two-ellipsoid menu to arbitrary block-specific spectral triples and any finite number of classes, proving an exact polynomial-size LP reduction and an attaining independent-sign product law. Recover the current piecewise formula as a symmetric two-class corollary.
